newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani stocks end up on cautious trading.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani stocks end up on cautious trading.

text.p: Pakistani stocks ended up on Monday, though off day's high, on cautious trading before Tuesday's settlement day, dealers said.

The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) 100-share index ended 4.96 points, or 0.31 percent, up at 1,593.61, after rising to 1,601.85 in early trading. Losers led gainers 235 to 90 in a turnover of 26.6 million shares, down from Friday's 34.5 million.
After a rise of some 10 points before midday, jobbers booked profits, prefering a safe exit in the absence of good corporate news, dealer Shaukat Hussain said.
A low turnover indicates that sellers are not interested in disposing off their holdings at these levels and buyers are in no mood to enhance their bids, one broker said.
HUBCO rose 0.50 to 38.30 rupees and Adamjee Insurance 3.00 to 108. Pakistan State Oil fell 2.00 to 300 and Dewan Salman Fibre 0.20 to 40.80. PTCL closed unchanged at 30.10.
